newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close up led by Teva.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close up led by Teva.

text.p: Tel Aviv shares closed higher on Monday led by a sharp rise in Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which reported strong third-quarter earnings, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.50 percent, or 0.96 points, to 192.43 on a low all-share turnover of 53 million shekels against 47 million on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index gained 0.51 percent to 202.20.
"Activity was mixed today and turnover continues to be low. Several stocks in the Maof moved sharply on very low volume," said Doron Tsur, head of research at Sahar Securities.
"Teva was the main contributor to the rise. The market is also waiting for (Friday's) release of October's consumer price index. Our forecast is that it will rise around 0.8 percent," Tsur added.

Teva, the most active share, rose 3.25 percent to 149,226 on volume of 6.3 million shekels. Teva's earnings per ADR rose in the third quarter to $0.39 from $0.32 a year earlier. Traders said the earnings were above expectations. Lehman Brothers had estimated earnings per ADR of $0.35.

Elite Industries rose 0.75 percent to 1,374 after Bank Hapoalim's securities department said the company's true value was $220 million to $240 million, against its current market value of $195 million.
Elco Industries fell 3.75 percent to 7,841 but traders noted that volume was very low at 110,000 shekels.

"Trading was very selective today with most of the activity concentrated in a few shares. Volume continues to be low and investors show no interest in the market," said a trader at the First International Bank of Israel.

Other active shares include Clal Industries, which rose 1.5 percent to 1,297 on volume of 5.4 million shekels and Koor Industries, which gained 1.0 percent to 28,602 on turnover of 2.4 million shekels.
